hints.title: Global Frequency Constraint Obstacle
hints.text: If a character appears fewer than k times in string s, can it ever be part of any valid valid substring? How does splitting around invalid characters reduce the problem?

hints.title: Split Divider Invariant
hints.text: Any character with frequency count < k in the current substring acts as a split divider. The longest valid substring must lie entirely within one of the separated parts.

hints.title: Divide and Conquer Procedure
hints.text: Count frequencies of all characters in s. Find the first character ch whose count is less than k. If no such character exists, return len(s). Otherwise, split s on ch and recursively return the maximum length across all split parts.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Divide and conquer recursion splitting on characters with frequency < k with depth bounded by 26 unique characters.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all O(N^2) substrings with frequency maps takes O(26 * N^2) which times out for N = 10^4.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Recursion stack depth bounded by alphabet size 26.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining why characters with count < k can never participate in any valid substring.
